Your post made me thing of something from a different sci-fi source. In the Ender's Game series there's a philosophy introduced called "The Hierarchy of Foreignness". It breaks all people into one of four categories. The first is called Utlanning and it is person on your planet and your species but from a different city or area. The Framling is someone of your race from a different planet. The Raman is the sentient alien species that we can communicate with and form treaties with. Last is the Varelse the sentient alien who is so foreign that meaningful communication is impossible. Nearly every Star Trek species is Raman in this classification but the Borg are Varelse. They cannot, will not communicate with another species and as posed by The Hierarchy of Foreignness war is only justifiable with Varelse, up to and including total xenocide. Now I find the Borg fascinating by looking at them through this philosophy, especially compared to Jean Luc. Jean Luc is the kind of captain who is determined to see all races as Raman. He wants to reason with them and come to an agreeable diplomatic solution. But here is a species that defies that world (universe?) view. With the Borg there is no diplomacy, with the Borg there is no treaty. With the Borg you must fight or die, and they are much much stronger than you. So not only does Picard have to abandon his diplomatic comfort zone he can't simply fight his way out either. I find it results in some really fun and interesting episodes. Granted all of this is my personal opinion and you are perfectly free to dislike the Borg, I just though you may find the Hierarchy of Foreignness interesting.
